idea: Real estate fund manager selection research for family offices
buyer: Family offices allocating to real estate funds
pain: They allocate to property funds without assessing the underlying assets
v1: One manager assessment including asset-level review
verdict: Her asset-level lens is a real differentiator in manager selection, but the buyer is reached by introduction.

why.distribution: Family offices via her husband's network; introductions rather than direct access.
why.demand: Inferred - allocators assess managers on process and returns, rarely on the buildings themselves.
why.fmf: Assessing the actual assets inside a property fund is something almost no allocator consultant can do.
why.defensibility: The asset-level capability is genuinely rare and would compound into a comparative dataset.
why.leverage: Bespoke per manager with site visits.
why.time_to_revenue: 3-6 months to build the first relationships.
why.tailwind: Family office growth is real but slow.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 assessments = £198k, requiring an allocator client base she does not have.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 assessments = £198k. Allocation decisions are infrequent per family office, so eighteen assessments needs 8-10 client relationships. Realistic: 3-4 = £33-44k.
carries: A genuinely rare capability - almost nobody assesses property funds at the building level.
kills: Demand is unproven and the allocation frequency per client is too low.
test: Ask three family offices how they assessed their last property fund allocation.
test_pass: They admit they never looked at the buildings.
test_fail: They rely on a consultant and are content.
